use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: To resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks which are being reported to the interface and are eligible for correlation.

goal.raw_text: To resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks which are being reported to the interface and are eligible for correlation.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU must have the capability to transmit and receive all response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks held locally.
All IUs must periodically compare remote tracks to local tracks (and optionally common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.

The frequency of comparisons, criteria for determining that two tracks represent the same object, and correlation rules must be in accordance with section 4.4.4.3.1, Air and Surface Track Correlation.
A C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

trigger.raw_text: A C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

claims.content: The C2 JU initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
The recognizing JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
The J7.2 message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

Receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
If the receiving IU has prespecified conditions that require or allow it to reject the requested correlation, it may reject the correlation request.

If the receiving IU desires to reverse the requested correlation and the originating JU’s J7.2 message has RV field set to 0 (indicating reverse correlation is acceptable), the receiving IU may originate a reverse correlation request.

If the receiving IU desires to reverse the requested correlation but the originating JU’s J7.2 message has RV field set to 1 (indicating reverse correlation would be rejected), the receiving IU must not originate a reverse correlation request and may instead reject the original correlation request.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the receiving IU shall transmit a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection.

If the correlation was manually initiated (RV field set to 3 in the J7.2 message), the receiving IU shall accept the correlation unless certain conditions apply which require rejection as specified in paragraph 4.7.3.2.c.
The dual designation is resolved, with one Track Number (TN) retained and the other TN dropped.
All receiving C² IUs have performed the correlation of the two tracks as requested in the J7.2 message, unless a rejection was transmitted.
If the correlation request was rejected, a J7.2 message with the Response Value (RV) field set to value 2 has been transmitted to report the rejection.
If a reverse correlation request was originated and accepted, the roles of the retained and dropped Track Numbers are reversed from the original request.
